title: Free and Fair Hardware: A Pathway to Copyright Infringement-Free Verilog Generation using LLMs
problem: Fine-tuned LLMs for hardware Verilog generation inherit copyright-protected code from training datasets, creating legal risk. Existing curated datasets lack licensing checks and scale limitations.
motivation: As Verilog code generation becomes more critical for hardware design automation, uncontrolled copyright infringement in fine-tuned models undermines the legitimate adoption of LLM-based design tools.
method: They create FreeSet, a dataset of 220k Verilog files automatically checked to ensure fair-use licensing compliance. A Llama model is then trained on FreeSet through continual pre-training (teaching an existing model new code while keeping its prior knowledge) to create FreeV. They then test FreeV's output against a benchmark that measures copyright violation risk in the generated Verilog code.
key_novelty: The key innovation is automatically checking copyright licenses in training data so that models trained on legally-approved code can generate new Verilog without risk of copyright infringement.
contributions: Evaluation benchmark for measuring copyright infringement risk in Verilog-trained LLMs
FreeSet: open-source dataset of 220k copyright-safe Verilog files with licensing framework
FreeV: Llama model trained on FreeSet achieving 3% copyright violation rate
10% improvement in VerilogEval pass@10 rates while minimizing IP risk
limitations: Evaluation focused on copyright detection; code correctness/synthesis validation against broader Verilog benchmarks not discussed.
